title: Geometry of finite roots for possibly disconnected SNC labels
statement:
Let $k$ be a field of characteristic a positive prime $p$, and let $V=\operatorname{Spec}B$ be a regular Noetherian affine $k$-scheme [def-weil-regular-scheme, def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions]. Let $t_1,\ldots,t_r\in B$, $r\geq0$, define a reduced strict normal crossings boundary $V(\prod_i t_i)$ [def-trf-strict-normal-crossings-boundary]. At every $v\in V$, assume that the labels vanishing at $v$ occupy distinct positions in a regular system of parameters of $\mathcal O_{V,v}$ [def-weil-pbc-regular-system-of-parameters]. Individual $V(t_i)$ may be disconnected or reducible. Put $f=\prod_i t_i$, with empty product $1$. For each $a\geq1$ prime to $p$, form the multivariate polynomial quotient [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring]
$$C_a=B[x_{1,a},\ldots,x_{r,a}]/(x_{i,a}^{a}-t_i)_i,\qquad X_a=\operatorname{Spec}C_a.$$
Then $C_a$ is finite free over $B$ with basis $\{\prod_i x_{i,a}^{e_i}:0\leq e_i<a\}$. For any $B$-algebra $R$, the canonical map identifies $R\otimes_B C_a$ with $R[x_{1,a},\ldots,x_{r,a}]/(x_{i,a}^{a}-t_i)_i$, fixing coefficients and the named root coordinates. For $a\mid b$, the substitutions $x_{i,a}\mapsto x_{i,b}^{b/a}$ define $B$-algebra maps $C_a\to C_b$; these maps are identity for $a=b$, compose by divisibility, and commute with these scalar-extension identifications [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product].
For every $v\in V$, set $I(v)=\{i:t_i(v)=0\}$. There is an affine neighbourhood $W$ of $v$ on which all inactive $t_j$ are units, and the nonempty closed subschemes $V(t_i)\cap W$ for $i\in I(v)$ are pairwise distinct reduced integral branches forming the restricted strict normal crossings boundary. For every $a$ as above, the algebra on $W$ adjoining only these active roots is regular Noetherian; the algebra adjoining all roots is also regular Noetherian. Globally $C_a$ is regular Noetherian and normal [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring]. Multiplication by $f$ is injective on both $B$ and $C_a$. Each $X_a$ has finitely many open and closed normal integral components, and $X_a^\circ=\operatorname{Spec}C_a[1/f]$ contains every generic point and is dense in each component [def-weil-ring-localization-away, def-pc-integral-scheme]. The zero ring, empty boundary, and $a=1$ are allowed.

proof.text: Treat $B=0$ directly as in step 11. Otherwise, for fixed $a$, set $A_0=B$ and $A_j=A_{j-1}[x_j]/(x_j^a-t_j)$ for $1\leq j\leq r$. Evaluation of the named variables in either direction identifies $A_r$ with $C_a$: the relations vanish and the composites fix coefficients and all variables. By [lem-weil-pbc-monic-quotient-free], every element of $A_j$ has a unique expression $\sum_{e_j<a}u_{e_j}x_j^{e_j}$ with $u_{e_j}\in A_{j-1}$. Induction starting with the basis $\{1\}$ of $A_0$ gives the asserted unique monomial expansion over $B$. Thus $C_a$ is finite free, and [lem-weil-pbc-finite-algebra-noetherian] makes it Noetherian. The same argument applies to any subfamily of the labels over any Noetherian coefficient ring.

source.place: Tag 04GG (lemma-characterize-henselian), proof of (10) implies (1), monic quotient basis; Tag 00FN (lemma-Noetherian-permanence). Iteration written out for the ILO IX 2.1 parameter-root presentation.

proof.text: Let $R$ be a $B$-algebra and put $D=R[y_1,\ldots,y_r]/(y_i^a-t_i)_i$. The tensor pushout [lem-weil-pbc-algebra-tensor-pushout-universal-property] defines $F:R\otimes_BC_a\to D$ by $F(u\otimes[P])=uP(y)$. Conversely evaluation gives $G:D\to R\otimes_BC_a$, fixing $R$ by $u\mapsto u\otimes1$ and sending $y_i$ to $1\otimes x_{i,a}$. It respects $y_i^a=t_i$ since $1\otimes t_i=t_i\otimes1$. The composite $FG$ fixes coefficients and variables, and $GF$ fixes $u\otimes1$ and $1\otimes x_{i,a}$, hence all tensors and their sums. They are inverse $R$-algebra maps. These are exactly the required scalar-extension identifications, retaining every named coordinate.

source.place: Tag 01I4 (lemma-fibre-product-affine-schemes), tensor pushout universal property; explicit polynomial-quotient inverse maps.

proof.text: For $a\mid b$, write $b=ah$. Substitution $x_{i,a}\mapsto x_{i,b}^h$ kills $x_{i,a}^a-t_i$, since $(x_{i,b}^h)^a=x_{i,b}^b=t_i$, and so induces the required algebra map. If $a=b$, $h=1$ and it fixes the generators. If $a\mid b\mid c$, the composite sends $x_{i,a}$ to $x_{i,c}^{(c/b)(b/a)}=x_{i,c}^{c/a}$; agreement on coefficients and variables proves composition. For any $B\to R$, both routes around the scalar-extension square fix $u\otimes1$ and send $1\otimes x_{i,a}$ to the same $y_{i,b}^{b/a}$. The tensor universal property proves that the square commutes.

source.place: IX Proposition 2.1 proof, printed p.133, simultaneous parameter-root algebra; divisibility substitutions and base-change compatibility made explicit.

proof.text: For each label put $D_i=\operatorname{Spec}(B/(t_i))$. Its coordinate ring is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-surjective-image-noetherian]. Identify the ambient stalk with $B_{\mathfrak p_w}$ using [lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-stalk-localization]. At $w\in D_i$ its local ring is $B_{\mathfrak p_w}/(t_i)$ by [lem-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime-of-quotient]. The hypothesis places $t_i$ in a regular parameter system of $B_{\mathfrak p_w}$, so [lem-weil-pbc-regular-local-generators-regular-sequence] makes this quotient regular local. Thus $D_i$ is a regular Noetherian scheme, including when it is empty. By [rem-pc-regular-normal](1),(2), $D_i$ is a finite disjoint union of open and closed normal integral components. This conclusion concerns each entire labelled vanishing locus; it does not assume it was an irreducible boundary component.

source.place: Tag 0BIA (lemma-strict-normal-crossings), regular parameter quotients; Algebra Tag 00NQ (lemma-regular-ring-CM); Properties Tag 033M (lemma-normal-Noetherian).

proof.text: Fix $v$. For every $i\in I(v)$ retain the unique component $E_i$ of $D_i$ containing $v$. Delete all other components of these finitely many $D_i$, and delete $D_j$ for $j\notin I(v)$. These are finitely many closed subsets of $V$, none containing $v$. By [lem-weil-pbc-affine-opens-basis] choose an affine open $W$ containing $v$ in their complement. Every inactive $t_j$ is invertible on $W$: it belongs to no maximal ideal of its coordinate ring. Also $D_i\cap W=E_i\cap W$ is nonempty integral and reduced. The branches are pairwise distinct: equality of two of them would give $(t_i)=(t_j)$ in $\mathcal O_{V,v}$, whereas after putting $t_i,t_j$ first in a parameter system, [lem-weil-pbc-regular-local-generators-regular-sequence] makes $t_j$ a nonzerodivisor on the nonzero ring $\mathcal O_{V,v}/(t_i)$; it therefore cannot be zero there. Their union is the restricted boundary since the deleted inactive labels are units. Restricting the supplied SNC boundary to $W$ preserves its regular-intersection and local dimension conditions, so these are exactly its reduced integral branches.

source.place: Tag 0BIA (lemma-strict-normal-crossings), identification of branches through a point with the distinct parameter primes; finite-component shrinking made explicit using Properties Tag 033M.

proof.text: For a prime $\mathfrak p\subset B$, put $R=B_{\mathfrak p}$, $d=\dim R$ and $S=\{i:t_i\in\mathfrak p\}$. The ring $R$ is regular local by [def-weil-regular-scheme], and its parameter hypothesis is identified with the given stalk hypothesis by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-stalk-localization]. For every $J\subseteq S$, put those distinct parameter positions first in a full parameter system. By [lem-weil-pbc-regular-local-generators-regular-sequence], $R/(t_j:j\in J)$ is regular local of dimension $d-|J|$. Thus all the hypotheses of [lem-sfb-transverse-local-root-family-regular] hold for the full finite family of labels at this prime. Since $(a,p)=1$, Bezout gives integers $u,v$ with $ua+vp=1$; characteristic $p$ gives $(u\cdot1_R)(a\cdot1_R)=1$. That lemma with its $J=\varnothing$ proves that, for every subset $K$ of the labels, the local-coefficient algebra $T_K=R[x_i:i\in K]/(x_i^a-t_i)_i$ is regular Noetherian. In particular it handles inactive units together with the ramified active roots, without a henselian or root-of-unity hypothesis.

source.place: IX Proposition 2.1 proof, printed p.133; local regularity input supplied by the existing transverse-root lemma, with its quotient/dimension hypotheses checked by Algebra Tag 00NQ.

proof.text: Here is the localization passage for any subfamily $K$. Write $C_K=B[x_i:i\in K]/(x_i^a-t_i)_i$ and $M=B\setminus\mathfrak p$. By step 2 and the fraction formulas, $M^{-1}C_K\cong T_K$: send $c/s$ to $(1/s)\otimes c$, with inverse $(b/s)\otimes c\mapsto bc/s$. These inverse formulas respect balancing and fraction equality. If $\mathfrak q\subset C_K$ contracts to $\mathfrak p$, its extension in this localization is the prime $Q=\{c/s:c\in\mathfrak q,s\in M\}$: denominators avoid $\mathfrak q$, so primality and membership follow by multiplying denominators. The maps between $(M^{-1}C_K)_Q$ and $(C_K)_{\mathfrak q}$ send $(c/s)/(e/t)$ to $ct/(se)$ and $c/e$ to $(c/1)/(e/1)$, respectively, where $e\notin\mathfrak q$. Their denominators are units and their composites fix every fraction. Thus $(C_K)_{\mathfrak q}\cong(T_K)_Q$. By step 6 the right side is regular local. Step 1 supplies Noetherianity, proving global regularity of every $C_K$, in particular $C_a$.

source.place: Tags 00CO (definition-localization), 00CP (proposition-universal-property-localization) and 00E3 (lemma-spec-localization); the coefficient and prime localization maps are written explicitly.

proof.text: Let $A=\Gamma(W,\mathcal O_W)$ for the neighbourhood in step 5. Its ring is Noetherian by [pqf-lem-affine-open-locnoeth], and its stalks agree with the stalks of $V$ by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-stalk-localization]. Hence $A$ is regular and the original hypothesis about each vanishing subtuple remains valid at every $w\in W$. Repeating steps 6 and 7 over $A$ proves regular Noetherianity both for $K=I(v)$ (the algebra adjoining just the roots labelled active at $v$) and for the full set of labels. The neighbourhood was chosen before $a$, so it works for every permitted $a$. Globally $C_a$ is regular Noetherian by step 7; [lem-weil-pbc-regular-ring-normal] therefore gives its asserted normality.

source.place: Tag 0567 (lemma-regular-normal); Properties Tag 01OW (lemma-locally-Noetherian). Application of the local root argument to an affine open.

proof.text: For a prime $\mathfrak p\subset B$: if $t_i\notin\mathfrak p$, its image is a unit. Otherwise put $t_i$ first in a parameter system; [lem-weil-pbc-regular-local-generators-regular-sequence] and [def-weil-pbc-regular-sequence] show that multiplication by it is injective. Thus multiplication by $f$ is injective in every $B_{\mathfrak p}$. If $fz=0$ in $B$, all $z/1$ vanish, and [lem-weil-pbc-prime-localizations-jointly-injective] gives $z=0$. Finally, write $z\in C_a$ uniquely in the monomial basis of step 1. The equation $fz=0$ says that $f$ kills every coefficient, so all coefficients are zero. This proves injectivity on $B$ and on $C_a$ without assuming either ring is a domain.

source.place: Tags 00NP (lemma-regular-domain), 00NQ (lemma-regular-ring-CM) and 00HN (lemma-characterize-zero-local), followed by the monic-basis coefficient calculation.

proof.text: By [rem-pc-regular-normal](1),(2), the regular Noetherian affine scheme $X_a$ is a finite disjoint union of open and closed normal integral components. By [lem-weil-pbc-spec-irreducible-components-minimal-primes], every component is $V(\mathfrak q)$ for a minimal prime $\mathfrak q$ of $C_a$. Its generic point is $\mathfrak q$ by the closure formula and uniqueness in [lem-weil-pbc-spec-irreducible-closed-subsets-primes]. By [lem-pc-minimal-prime-avoids-nonzerodivisor] and step 9, $f\notin\mathfrak q$. Thus every such generic point belongs to $D(f)$. The principal open $D(f)$ is $\operatorname{Spec}C_a[1/f]$ by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-ideals-closed-subscheme](0). Its intersection with each component contains that component's generic point, so its closure in the component is the whole component by [def-sc-generic-point]. This is exactly the required componentwise density.

source.place: Tag 033M (lemma-normal-Noetherian); density by the minimal-prime/nonzerodivisor statement of Mathlib notMem_nonZeroDivisors_of_mem_mem_minimalPrimes (Mathlib/RingTheory/Ideal/MinimalPrime/Localization.lean:97), and the generic-point closure formula.

proof.text: If $B=0$, every root algebra and its scalar extensions are zero; a $B$-algebra is necessarily zero. Its monomial expansion is still unique, all multiplication maps on its singleton underlying set are injective, and the pointwise and component assertions are vacuous. If $r=0$, the root algebra is $B$, its basis is $\{1\}$, $f=1$, all transitions are identities and the boundary is empty. One may choose $W=V$; the component and density assertions follow from step 10 with $D(1)=X_a$. For $a=1$, evaluation $x_{i,1}\mapsto t_i$ identifies $C_1$ with $B$ and every formula above specializes to this identification. These cases require no nonempty boundary or positive dimension.

The statement is unchanged, there are no new nodes, and no repair note names this item. Step 4: each D_i is regular Noetherian, by the parameter quotient and the stalk/quotient localizations, and splits into finitely many clopen normal integral components (rem-pc-regular-normal (1),(2)). Step 5: the shrinking to W is correct: the removed sets are closed, inactive labels become units, and branches are distinct because t_j is a nonzerodivisor on the nonzero ring O/(t_i). I also checked that no branch can contain another (both are height-one primes) and that the SNC conditions are pointwise, so they restrict to W. Step 6: all hypotheses of lem-sfb-transverse-local-root-family-regular hold, including R/(t_J) regular of dimension d-|J| for every J in S, and a is a unit by Bezout in characteristic p. Steps 7-8: localization to the global and W-level regularity, then normality. Steps 9-10: f is a nonzerodivisor (unit or first parameter at each prime, then joint injectivity of localizations, then coefficientwise on the basis), so f misses every minimal prime and D(f) is dense in each component. Step 11: B=0, r=0 and a=1 are correct. I also tested k[u] with t=u(u-1), and k[u,v] with labels u,v.
